/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
import base64, textwrap
script = r'''
import os, re, subprocess, sys, zipfile
from pathlib import Path

animals_zip = sys.argv[1]
fungi_zip = sys.argv[2]
out_path = Path(sys.argv[3])
work = Path('rcv_work')
work.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
float_re = re.compile(r'[-+]?(?:\\d*\\.\\d+|\\d+\\.?)(?:[eE][-+]?\\d+)?')

def rcv_for_file(path):
    commands = [
        ['phykit', 'rcv', str(path)],
        ['phykit', 'relative_composition_variability', str(path)],
    ]
    last_error = None
    for cmd in commands:
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
        if proc.returncode == 0:
            text = (proc.stdout + '\\n' + proc.stderr).strip()
            nums = float_re.findall(text)
            if not nums:
                raise RuntimeError('No numeric RCV value found in output for %s: %s' % (path, text))
            return nums[-1]
        last_error = proc.stderr.strip() or proc.stdout.strip()
    raise RuntimeError('PhyKIT rcv failed for %s: %s' % (path, last_error))

def iter_scores(label, archive_path):
    rows = []
    target_dir = work / label
    target_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as zf:
        names = sorted(n for n in zf.namelist() if n.endswith('.faa.mafft') and not n.endswith('/'))
        for i, name in enumerate(names, 1):
            data = zf.read(name)
            ortholog = Path(name).name[:-len('.faa.mafft')]
            aln_path = target_dir / ('%05d_%s.faa.mafft' % (i, ortholog))
            aln_path.write_bytes(data)
            rows.append((label, ortholog, rcv_for_file(aln_path)))
    return rows

rows = []
rows.extend(iter_scores('animal', animals_zip))
rows.extend(iter_scores('fungal', fungi_zip))
if not rows:
    raise RuntimeError('No .faa.mafft alignments found')
with out_path.open('w') as out:
    out.write('group\\tortholog\\trcv\\n')
    for group, ortholog, value in rows:
        out.write('%s\\t%s\\t%s\\n' % (group, ortholog, value))
'''.strip() + '\\n'
print(base64.b64encode(script.encode()).decode())
PY"
